1. Case 1: Metastatic pleural malignancy
The patient's chronic right pleuritic pain and progressive dyspnoea, exudative pleural fluid with markedly elevated LDH/ADA, thickened pleura on CT and ultrasound, and negative cultures strongly support malignant pleural disease. The absence of fever/cough and negative cultures make chronic infection and tuberculous effusion unlikely; prior trauma and treated effusion leave post-traumatic pleural sequelae as secondary. Within malignancy, no asbestos exposure refutes mesothelioma and supports metastatic pleural malignancy as the leading subtype, while primary pleural lymphoma remains rare. Definitive confirmation awaits pleural fluid cytology and biopsy pathology, so confidence is moderate.
